---
title: "Paired RNA and ATAC with WNN"
---

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(error = FALSE, collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
```

## Scope

This small example executes weighted nearest-neighbor analysis on 80 paired
cells from the packaged `pbmcmultiome_sub` object. It needs no downloaded
fragments, reference sequence or Python environment. The subset and small
feature/dimension settings illustrate the interface; they are not recommended
parameters for a complete biological analysis.

WNN combines RNA and ATAC neighborhoods. It does not correct sample batch
effects. Supplying `batch` emits a warning rather than silently implying that
correction occurred. Review batch effects separately before interpreting joint
clusters. See [WNN_integrate()](../reference/WNN_integrate.html) for the method contract.

## Run paired preprocessing and WNN

```{r paired-wnn}
data("pbmcmultiome_sub", package = "scop")
paired <- subset(pbmcmultiome_sub, cells = colnames(pbmcmultiome_sub)[1:80])
paired <- scop::WNN_integrate(
  srt_merge = paired, assay = c("RNA", "peaks"),
  linear_reduction_dims = 10, linear_reduction_dims_use = 2:8,
  nHVF = 100, neighbor_k = 10, nonlinear_reduction_dims = 2,
  verbose = FALSE
)
SeuratObject::Reductions(paired)
```

Explicit assay selection keeps derived `chromvar` and `ACTIVITY` assays out of
the RNA input. Custom RNA assay names must be supplied explicitly. Gene
activity is an accessibility-derived proxy, and chromVAR measures motif-related
accessibility deviations; neither is measured RNA.

## Inspect reusable outputs

Both the default append mode and `append = FALSE` retain the RNA PCA, ATAC LSI,
WNN graphs, modality weights and clustering results. The reduction receipt
records the actual cells, peaks and selected dimensions at calculation time.

```{r inspect-results}
paired@misc$WNN_reduction_list
paired@misc$WNN_dims_list
stopifnot(all(paired@misc$WNN_reduction_list %in% SeuratObject::Reductions(paired)))
head(paired[[]][, c("RNA.weight", "ATAC.weight", "WNNclusters")])
SeuratObject::Misc(paired[["ATAClsi"]], "scop_atac_representation")$dimensions
```

```{r joint-embedding, fig.width=6, fig.height=4}
Seurat::DimPlot(paired, reduction = "WNNUMAP2D", group.by = "WNNclusters")
```

For the common dispatcher, use `RunIntegration(srt_merge = paired,
batch = NULL, integration_methods = "WNN", assay = c("RNA", "peaks"), ...)` with the same
analysis parameters. Native counts remain available for a subsequent
[RunLinkPeaks()](../reference/RunLinkPeaks.html) analysis, which additionally requires compatible gene
coordinates and verified sequence statistics. WNN clusters and peak-gene
associations do not by themselves establish causal regulation.
